title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence
status: Working paper; August 12 revision; institutional primary abstract
data_design: ADP payroll through June 2026; occupation exposure; ages 22–25
finding: Reports a 19% relative employment shortfall among exposed early-career workers, without economy-wide displacement.
relevance_limit: A stock comparison motivates the question; it does not by itself identify entry, downgrading, or our CPS estimand.

title: Generative AI as Seniority-Biased Technological Change: Evidence from U.S. Résumé and Job Posting Data
status: Working paper; revised primary SSRN abstract located; full-text fetch restricted
data_design: US resumes and AI-integrator posting signals; firm adoption comparison
finding: The revised abstract associates adoption with weaker junior employment, chiefly slower hiring.
relevance_limit: Seniority is not age; adoption signals, selected firms and pretrends differ from exposure-only public surveys. No inaccessible revised coefficient is quoted.

title: You’re (not) Hired: Artificial Intelligence and Early Career Hiring in the Quarterly Workforce Indicators
status: CES working paper 26-27; April; primary PDF
data_design: Administrative QWI tabulations; ages 22–24; industry exposure
finding: Documents early-career weakness in exposed industries and examines hiring as a margin.
relevance_limit: Industry exposure and published age bins differ from our occupational Q5; new-hire counts and rates are distinct.

title: Graduating into Disruption: Labor Market Outcomes for AI-Exposed College Majors
status: CES working paper 26-56; September; primary PDF
data_design: Graduate administrative records; predetermined major exposure
finding: Top-exposure majors show a 5-pp initial employment decline and 13% lower initial full-quarter earnings.
relevance_limit: Graduates and majors define a different risk set; sector reallocation and within-sector earnings both matter.

title: Still waters, rapid currents: Early labor market transformation under generative AI
status: Author-written October 6 research synthesis of the adoption study
data_design: 25,000 Danish workers, 11 occupations; administrative records through December 2024
finding: Reports precise average earnings/hours nulls, task changes, and occupational mobility; adopting firms do not drive the early-career decline.
relevance_limit: Country institutions and follow-up differ. This version rules out average effects above 2%; do not mix older 1% abstract bounds.

title: What We Do and Don’t Know About How AI is Affecting the Labor Market
data_design: US CPS; synthetic DID and comparison of cyclical sensitivity
finding: Finds no clear labor-market effect in its design and stresses baseline differences between exposed and unexposed occupations.
relevance_limit: Motivates longer preperiods and recovery controls; non-detection is not proof of no harm.

title: Young workers’ employment drops in occupations with high AI exposure
data_design: CPS; ages 20–24 versus 25–55; entry and exit comparisons
finding: Highlights reduced inflows from nonparticipation rather than increased layoffs in young exposed occupations.
relevance_limit: Different age band, exposure measure and risk set; explicitly uncertain causality. Our controlled entry test does not reproduce a resolved extra Q5 decline.

title: How Does AI Change Labor Demand? Evidence from 41 Countries
data_design: Multinational affiliates; adoption signals and instrumented event study
finding: Junior share falls 1.9 pp, mainly because senior employment rises; the junior headcount decrease is insignificant.
relevance_limit: Relative shares need not imply absolute job destruction. The IV exclusion restriction and multinational selection remain substantive assumptions.

title: Generative AI at Work
data_design: Staggered assistant rollout at a customer-support firm
finding: Documents productivity gains and heterogeneous worker benefits.
relevance_limit: Firm productivity gains do not establish aggregate employment effects, welfare gains for every worker, or age-specific displacement.

title: Estimating gross flows consistent with stocks in the CPS
status: BLS Monthly Labor Review; primary methodological article
data_design: CPS rotation overlap, classification errors and stock-consistent flow estimation
finding: Explains why matched flows need not reproduce stock changes and describes margin adjustment.
relevance_limit: Matching margins is an accounting constraint, not verification of unobserved individual transitions.

title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
data_design: Human and GPT-4 task ratings; potential time savings
finding: Defines a task-based exposure rubric rather than an adoption or displacement estimate.
relevance_limit: Potential task exposure must remain separate from realized employment effects.

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
status: Primary METR research release; benchmark background
data_design: Human task duration and model completion curves
relevance_limit: Transfer from software benchmarks to occupational tasks is a modeling assumption, not a workplace success probability.
